issues.issue: Does a breach of the stay condition date to the offence or to the conviction, for section 197?
issues.applicant_position: Breach occurred when the offence was committed, before the IRPA took effect, so s.197 should not apply.
issues.respondent_position: Breach is dated to the conviction, after the IRPA took effect, so s.197 applies.
issues.result_quote: The appropriate interpretation of the time of breach, as regards section 197 of the IRPA, is the time of the offence.

issues.issue: Does section 197 apply retrospectively to an offence committed before the IRPA, and does the presumption against retrospectivity bar it?
issues.applicant_position: Section 197 covers only breaches after the IRPA came into force, so it cannot reach this offence.
issues.result_quote: section 197 is clearly intended to be retrospective and, in any event, the presumption against retrospectivity does not apply to this protective legislation.

issues.issue: Does a conviction after the IRPA came into force count as a second breach that triggers s.197 on its own?
issues.respondent_position: Conviction is a second breach after the IRPA took effect, so s.197 applies even without retrospectivity.
issues.result_quote: In light of the reasoning above, it is not strictly necessary to deal with this argument.
